headline: WTI under $90, Saudi pipeline restarting, US-Iran met 3 hours, Nasdaq record again
stance: Supply is coming back before the war ends. The front end moved on it Tuesday; the long end did not.

news.head: Saudi Arabia restarts the East-West pipeline
news.body: Reported Tuesday. The line is running at a low rate against a 4m b/d target. Riyadh is aiming for meaningful flows by Saturday.

news.head: US and Iran met three hours in New York
news.body: Trump called it very good Tuesday. Iranian state TV said Araghchi met Witkoff on the UN sidelines. Another meeting is scheduled.

news.head: Trump threatens annihilation, defers any deal
news.body: In his UN address Tuesday. Iran can rebuild under a deal, he said, but not before the November midterms. Iran's delegation walked out.

implications: The premium is leaving crude without the war ending. Grains and copper still price the disruption at three-year extremes.
Cheaper crude reached the 2-year Tuesday and stopped there. The long end has not taken any of it.

watch.head: Pezeshkian addresses the UN, this morning
watch.body: Iran's president speaks in New York while the war runs. Any line on the strait or the talks hits crude before it hits rates.

watch.head: East-West pipeline ramp toward Saturday
watch.body: Riyadh is targeting meaningful flows by then. Loading rates at Yanbu are the read, not the headline.

watch.head: Follow-up US-Iran meeting, no date set
watch.body: Trump said another is scheduled in the very near future. A confirmed date is the next leg out of the crude premium.

watch.head: Jobless claims, Sep 24, 8:30
watch.body: The next US release. Nothing on the calendar today.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The front end took the crude move Tuesday. Monday the long end rallied and the 2-year sat still.
Natural gas $3.174, +11.9%, Tuesday's close. Specs sit extended short at the 3rd percentile, eight weeks running.
The US calendar is empty today. Rates trade New York headlines until jobless claims, Sep 24.
sections.positioning: September 15 report: specs went extended long Canadian dollar, 88th percentile, new this week. That is the oil currency, into a 10% crude slide.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: Nasdaq-100 set a second straight record close Tuesday. The S&P closed flat and is still below its August 13 high.
Nasdaq breadth is doing the work: 45.5% of members above their 50-day, from 38.6% Monday. S&P breadth went nowhere.
Banks are at their weakest against the S&P since June 3. Two records in two sessions, and financials are in neither.
sections.positioning: VIX specs sit extended short, 13th percentile on the September 15 report, six weeks there. Standing background, not a new lean.

single_name.note: Global Partners: insider buying filed September 21, trading above its 200-day. 3.8 days to cover. Fuel terminals, into a crude slide.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High yield kept tightening into Monday, straight through the crude slide. Credit has not traded either side of this war.
Reverse repo is effectively empty into the September 30 quarter turn. No buffer in the facility for that date.

ideas.line: 6 open · 1 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
